intro:
Use it for any list where the order is the point: a fitness challenge, a sales team's month, a game's weekly XP, the fastest times on a course. You pass entries with a value, and the component sorts them, numbers the places and draws the top three on a podium above the rest.

The component works out the ranks, so the data does not carry them. Entries on the same value share a place and the next place is skipped (1, 2, 2, 4), which is how a scoreboard is normally read.

**It renders every row it is given.** It is not virtualised, so for a long board pass `limit` and let `highlightId` keep the viewer's own row in view.

For one number and its trend, use [Kpi](/docs/components/kpi). For positions that change over several periods, use [BumpChart](/docs/charts/bump-chart).
usage:
<Leaderboard
  data={[
    { id: 'maya', name: 'Maya Chen', value: 84210, change: 2 },
    { id: 'omar', name: 'Omar Haddad', value: 79655 },
    { id: 'lena', name: 'Lena Brandt', value: 71038, change: -1 },
    { id: 'sam', name: 'Sam Okafor', value: 66402, change: 1 },
    { id: 'ines', name: 'Inès Moreau', value: 61987, change: -2 },
  ]}
  unit="steps"
/>

examples.title: Podium bars to scale
examples.description: The default podium. Each bar is drawn against the leader's value, so a close race looks close and a runaway looks like one. A floor keeps third place visible as a bar when the leader is far ahead. Set `podiumScale="rank"` to step the heights by place instead.

examples.title: Cards instead of bars
examples.description: `podium="cards"` gives each of the top three a card, with first raised between the other two. Use it when the values are labels people read — revenue, a level — rather than amounts to compare by eye. `formatValue` controls how the value is written, and the screen reader hears the same text.

examples.title: Keeping the viewer in sight
examples.description: `highlightId` tints that entry's row. When `limit` cuts it off, the row is pinned under the list with its real place, after a break that shows rows were skipped.

examples.title: Lowest first, for times
examples.description: `order="asc"` ranks the smallest value first, for a race time or a golf score. The podium then always steps by place, because a bar scaled to a winning time would be the shortest. `podium="none"` puts everyone in the list.
examples.code:
const lap = (s: number) => `${Math.floor(s / 60)}:${(s % 60).toFixed(2).padStart(5, '0')}`;

<Leaderboard data={laps} order="asc" podium="none" formatValue={lap} />

examples.title: Movement and presses
examples.description: `change` is the number of places an entry moved since the last period: positive is up the board, negative is down, 0 shows a dash. Leave it out and no movement column is drawn. `onPressEntry` makes every row and podium place a button, and receives the entry and its rank.
examples.code:
<Leaderboard
  data={[
    { id: 'a', name: 'Priya Nair', value: 412, change: 3, subtitle: 'Design' },
    { id: 'b', name: 'Tomás Ruiz', value: 398, change: 0, subtitle: 'Platform' },
    { id: 'c', name: 'Aiko Tanaka', value: 377, change: -2, subtitle: 'Growth' },
  ]}
  onPressEntry={(entry, rank) => router.push(`/people/${entry.id}`)}
/>

examples.title: A short list
examples.description: With three entries and `podium="none"`, everyone sits in the list. `subtitle` adds a second line under the name.
examples.code:
<Leaderboard
  podium="none"
  data={[
    { id: 'a', name: 'Priya Nair', value: 412, change: 3, subtitle: 'Design' },
    { id: 'b', name: 'Tomás Ruiz', value: 398, change: 0, subtitle: 'Platform' },
    { id: 'c', name: 'Aiko Tanaka', value: 377, change: -2, subtitle: 'Growth' },
  ]}
  unit="points"
/>

examples.title: Nothing to rank
examples.description: An empty `data` array shows `emptyText` in place of the board. It defaults to "No entries yet".
examples.code: <Leaderboard data={[]} emptyText="Nobody has logged a run this week" />

notes:
### Accessibility

Each podium place and each row is a single accessible element, read as one sentence: "Rank 2, Omar Haddad, 79,655 steps, up 1 place". A tie adds "tied" after the rank. Pass `unit` so the value is read with what it counts; without it, the reader hears a bare number.

### Reduced motion

The podium bars grow on mount, third place first and the leader last. With reduce motion on, they are drawn at full height straight away.

### Colour

The podium uses the theme's primary colour at three strengths rather than gold, silver and bronze. Fixed medal colours would clash with most of the themes, and the place is already shown by the number on the bar.

versions.title: Step challenge
versions.description: The bar podium, scaled to the values. Switching weeks swaps the data and the bars regrow to the new totals.
versions.code:
const [week, setWeek] = useState('this');

<Tabs value={week} onValueChange={setWeek}>
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="this">This week</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="last">Last week</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
</Tabs>
<Leaderboard
  data={week === 'this' ? thisWeek : lastWeek}
  unit="steps"
  podiumHeight={140}
/>
